_comment: The builder's field guide: how things are done here, in his voice, read at the reading stand in the study or from the copy in the wardrobe. Not the journal (his story, data/journal.json). Each page shows once its `after` flag is set (no `after`: from the start), so nothing ahead is told; a page not yet seen is marked new. `section` groups the contents. Every number, recipe and place here is the code's: change one, change the other (tests/fieldguide.test.ts checks the ones that can drift, and that every `after` flag is one the game sets).

pages.title: Getting out, and home
pages.text:
The way out is under the waterfall, across the valley on its west wall. Swim straight through the white water and down to the lamp over the tunnel, low in the rock. The tunnel is lit, and one breath will do it. Halfway along is my gate: swim up to it and it lifts by itself, and shuts behind you.

You come up in the canyon pool. Do not follow the stream down the canyon bed. On the far side of the pool from the falls, a grey gravel path zig-zags up the canyon's west wall. At its top the old road begins, and runs west.

If you are ever lost out there, hold the H key and you are home. The next page says when it works.

pages.title: Holding H for home
pages.text:
Hold the H key for two seconds, from anywhere, and you are home where you wake: the bed you last slept in, else the balcony. Nothing is lost and the clock does not move.

It will not start if something has hurt you in the last ten seconds, and a blow, a shot or a fall while you hold it stops it: get clear first. Hunger, thirst and holding your breath do not stop it. Opening a screen or sitting down lets it go.

One thing it does not do: a run that ends with H is not walking home, so it does not count for the first trip out (M1). Swim and walk that one yourself.

pages.title: If you fall out there
pages.text:
In the valley nothing is lost: you wake at the cave, as hungry and thirsty as you were. Eat and drink.

Outside it, everything you carried is left where you fell, in a sack, and you wake at home with nothing. The sack never goes away: go back for it, right-click it and take it all back. Anything half done on that trip (the gate, Zone 1) has to be done again.

So before a long trip, leave at home what you cannot bear to fetch.

pages.title: What I carry
pages.text:
Left of the first slot is the bare hand (the key left of 1). The clock beside it tells the hour: from five in the evening it turns warm, and a bed can be slept in until six in the morning. A day here passes in about twenty minutes.

With the bow or a gun in hand, the Q key slows the world for up to four seconds; it takes about twelve to come back. The binoculars: hold them and hold the right mouse button to look, let go to lower them.

The headlamp and the water filter work from the pack, just carried. The expedition backpack is different: hold it and right-click once, and the pack has nine more slots. All four are in the expedition kit in the vault.

pages.title: Water
pages.text:
The valley's water comes up through the limestone, and it is clean: the pool, the creek, the falls. With an empty hand (the key left of 1) right-click any water to drink, or hold an empty jug and right-click water to fill it. A jug drunk gives the jug back.

Outside the valley the water is not clean. A drink still quenches, but it turns the stomach and costs some health, and I would not fill a jug with it. My water filter makes it safe: it only has to be in your pack. It is in the expedition kit, in the vault.

pages.title: The garden
pages.text:
The steel hoe is on the tool wall in the workshop. Hold it and right-click grass, dirt or forest floor to till it; it clears tall grass, ferns and flowers as it goes. Then hold seeds and right-click the top of the tilled soil. The seed chest is in the pantry.

Crops want light (the sun, or a lantern close by), and they grow only while I am somewhere near them: about a quarter of an hour from seed to harvest. A night's sleep moves them on too. Mine a ripe crop and it gives its crop and seeds back, two of most, one of herbs. Potatoes grow from a potato. Mine one too early and you get a seed back, nothing more.

pages.title: Coffee, and bananas
pages.text:
The bushes along the south side of the garden carry red cherries when ripe. Right-click a ripe bush to pick three beans: the bush stays and ripens again. Do not dig it up. A bean sown in tilled soil grows into a new bush.

To brew, right-click the range on the balcony or the fireplace: three beans and a jug of water make three cups, and the jug comes back. A cup takes the edge off thirst and puts a spring in your step for a minute and a half.

The banana plants work the same way: right-click a yellow bunch for four bananas, and a green one hangs in its place and yellows in a few hours.

pages.title: Cooking, and food
pages.text:
Raw meat or fish will keep you going, but only just: a raw trout is worth a mouthful, cooked it is a meal. Right-click the range on the balcony or the fireplace to cook. Trout, rabbit, venison, pork and chicken cook one for one; two eggs make fried eggs; corn and salt make rice; bean pods and water make beans; potato, corn, tomato and herbs make a stew.

Nothing here spoils. What is in the pantry and the pack keeps as long as you need it. To eat, hold the food and right-click. The trout in the pool take a rod (on the tool wall): right-click the water to cast, and again when one bites.

pages.title: Sleep, and the night
pages.text:
A bed can be slept in from five in the evening until six in the morning: right-click it. You wake at six with some health back and a little hungrier, and the garden near you has grown as if the night had passed. The coop, the hutch and the jerky rack do their morning's work.

Sleep in my bed, through the double door on the cave's south side, and you wake at its foot from then on. A bed you make yourself (three planks, two cordage and eight plant fibre at the workbench) will do too.

Outside the valley, the night is when things hunt. Be home by dark until you know the road.

pages.title: The workshop and my handbooks
pages.text:
The workshop is through the hall at the back of the cave: the workbench, the smelter, the kiln, the anvil and the tannery rack. Right-click one to see what it makes; the E key shows what you can make by hand.

My handbooks stand beside the journal on the bookshelves: read them once (right-click the shelves) and the smelter, the kiln, the anvil and the tannery show their work. The kiln burns logs to charcoal and sand to glass; the smelter makes iron from the pantry wall's ore with charcoal; the anvil makes nails, tools, lanterns, arrowheads and arrows.

Some things show greyed out, with the milestone that opens them. They come in their time.

pages.title: Snares, and rabbits
pages.text:
Rabbits live past the canyon, east of the saddle, and come out by day. A snare (two sticks and two cordage at the workbench make two) set on the ground there catches one alive, but only while you are about. Traps cannot be set in the valley.

When it rustles, right-click the caught snare: the rabbit goes into your pack, and the snare is set again.

A hutch (six planks, four sticks and four nails at the workbench) at home with two or more rabbits in it gains one every morning, up to eight. Right-click it and put them in.

pages.title: Chickens, and the coop
pages.text:
There are hens loose by day at the farm on the old road; one more turns up each day. Walk right up to one (do not run, or she runs too) and right-click to catch her; she goes into your pack. Two make a pair.

The coop is made at the workbench: six planks, two wire mesh and eight nails. The barn's crates have the mesh. Set it down at home, right-click it, and put the hens in (shift-click moves them from your pack). With a pair in it, each hen lays an egg every morning, up to eight waiting, and the coop gives a feather.

Leave an egg in overnight and it may hatch: one more hen, up to eight. Your hens walk about the coop; right-click one to pick her up again.

pages.title: Keeping meat
pages.text:
Nothing spoils, but smoked meat and jerky feed far better than raw.

The smoker (six cobble, four planks and six nails at the workbench) needs wood as well as meat: right-click it and put in raw meat and some fuel (a log, planks, sticks or charcoal). Every four hours of the clock each piece of fuel smokes four pieces of meat.

The jerky rack (three planks and two cordage) needs no fuel: hang raw meat on it and by morning it is jerky.

pages.title: New crops
pages.text:
Marco sells quinoa seed, six for a few coins. The old apple tree in the farmyard's south-east corner, past the barn, gives a slip: right-click its trunk (one slip at a time). Plant either in tilled soil. A ripe apple tree is picked with a right-click, three apples, and it fruits again.

Raised beds (two planks and a cordage make two) are tilled soil you can set down anywhere. Later the planter boxes do the same on stone.

pages.title: Hides and leather
pages.text:
Most animals out there give a hide: rabbits, deer, boar, dogs, coyotes. At the tannery rack in the workshop a hide and a pinch of salt make two leather; a big cat's pelt makes more. The pantry has salt.

Six leather and two cordage at the workbench make leather armour: carried in the pack, it takes some of the sting out of every blow.

pages.title: Marco
pages.text:
Take the old road west from the top of the canyon path, up over the saddle between two knolls. Just past it, on the road's north side, is a bus shelter with its lantern lit. His number is scratched on the timetable: stand there and it is in my satellite phone.

The phone is on the desk in the study, and it only works from the valley. Call him and he will meet you at the shelter by daylight, from seven in the morning until six in the evening; after dark he waits for morning. Right-click him to trade. He pays half what a thing is worth, and says so, and he carries only so much coin a day.

He is paid from, and pays into, the hot wallet: the phone shows it. The cold wallet in the safe stays cold. You do not need it to trade.

pages.title: Marco's guns
pages.text: Now he trusts me he sells real things: a pistol, the raiders' rifle, pistol and rifle rounds, and primers by the ten. They are dear; rounds you make yourself go further.

pages.title: Doc
pages.text: Dr. Ibáñez answers the satellite phone, from the cave like Marco. Call him and pay from the hot wallet: his wound care puts your health back as far as your dose allows, and his treatment takes the dose away altogether, for more.

pages.title: Ray
pages.text: Ray Quispe was the dam's engineer: his number was in the logbook. Call him from the cave. He sells his drawings for a hydro generator, and parts: steel, graphics cards, power supplies, boards, wiring. Once a generator turns in the creek, call him again.

pages.title: Weapons, and hunting
pages.text:
The armory chest in the vault holds my rifle and forty rounds, the bow and thirty arrows, a machete and the vest. Left-click strikes with what is in your hand. The rifle fires with a right-click, and hits hard.

With a bow, hold the right mouse button to draw and let go to loose: a full draw takes a second and hits half again as hard as a snatched one, and more. An arrow into a man who has not seen you does three times the harm. Walk over a spent arrow to pick it up.

The vest takes nearly a third off every blow, and it only has to be in your pack. Deer bolt when you come near; a boar charges if you come close or hurt it. Both give meat and a hide.

pages.title: Bows and arrows
pages.text:
Four arrows at the workbench: two sticks, four arrowheads, and a plant fibre or a feather. At the anvil (once my handbooks are read) a flint will do for the heads. Arrowheads: a bone at the workbench makes two; an iron ingot makes six at the anvil.

A bow of your own is three sticks and a bowstring, once the first trip is done. Bowstrings I could never make: you will have to find them.

pages.title: Between the canyon and the saddle
pages.text:
The land from the canyon to the saddle is quiet by day: rabbits, deer, a boar or two. Give a boar room.

At night a puma hunts it. It circles to your back. Turn and face it, with nothing between you, and it stops; hold it in your eye long enough and it gives up. Let it close and it rushes. Better: be home by dark.

pages.title: Zone 1: the farm, and the dogs
pages.text:
Past the saddle the danger rises, and more at night. The farm off the road's south side has hens in the yard, the barn's crates, the old apple tree, and three dogs living in the house. Killed, they stay dead.

When a dog crouches and snarls it is about to spring: step back, then strike (left-click). They climb a single step and no more, and a bite cannot reach two blocks up: get up on a rock, a wall or a pillar of blocks and strike down at them.

At night coyotes run the road in twos and threes, from the sides. Step back when one crouches. A gunshot brings anything angry near it running, and scatters the rest.

pages.title: The outpost
pages.text:
Three of them hold the old tienda south of the road: a lookout with a rifle on the roof watching the road east, a man with a pistol behind the sandbags, a man with a machete in the doorway. None of them sees behind him.

The quiet way: leave the road east of it, where a game trail goes south through tall brush, round to the back. A blade (the knife, the machete, a spear) into a man who has not been alarmed is silent, and the others hear nothing. Crates against the back wall step up to the roof.

If they see you: every shot comes after an aim. A glint on the roof, or a click, means get behind something solid. A shot anywhere near wakes all three. Once quiet, they stay quiet: search the back room, and mine the forge to take it home.

pages.title: The forge
pages.text:
The raiders' forge comes away with a pickaxe as a set of forge parts. At the workbench four stone bricks, six planks, eight nails and the parts make a forge, and a tool rack with it. Set it in the workshop.

At the forge three scrap and a coal or charcoal make two iron; one iron makes eight arrowheads or twelve nails. Later it casts bullets.

pages.title: The hunters' camp, and the mine
pages.text:
The trail north from the antlered post (COTO DE CAZA) leads to the camp. The lodge has a chest; hides hang curing in the drying shed (mine them for leather); a rusted trap lies by the shed (right-click it to learn how it is made).

The jaguar is not looking for a fight. Keep five paces off and do not shoot near it, and it goes. If it does turn: step back when it crouches, then strike, and expect to be hurt.

The old mine south of the road is lit all the way down; its chamber walls are thick with iron and coal.

pages.title: The leghold trap
pages.text: Two iron, four nails and a cordage at the workbench make one. Set it outside the valley where deer or boar walk. One that steps in is held for a minute: go and finish it, and its meat and hide go to your pack. The trap stays set; mine it to take it up.

pages.title: Zone 2: faction ground
pages.text:
The highway north from the hunters' camp is lit all the way to Las Cruces. Two patrols walk it, a sentry walks the ruins, and two guards stand in the gate towers. They shoot strangers.

The scout's armband, carried, passes you for one of theirs from more than fourteen paces. Closer, they take a second look: back off, or fight. A shot near them, or hurting one, ends the pretence for that visit. Those you kill are replaced by the next dawn.

Las Cruces itself is reinforced concrete: no way in, and no tool touches it. Go round.

pages.title: The ruins
pages.text: Mine what was left: solar panels off the roofs, cable trays for wiring, copper pipe, car batteries for lead, the supermarket's fridges. In the exchange the server racks give graphics cards, power supplies and boards, and the UPS cabinets battery cells. The hardware store's stock has a pump unit, casings and primers. The pharmacy is the first shop you reach walking north: right-click its counter.

pages.title: Radiation, and the dose
pages.text:
Yellow signs and tape ring the hot places. Stay outside them. Inside, the dose climbs, and the meter shows how fast and how long to the limit.

The dose caps your health (never below forty) until it fades, about four a day, wherever you are. Past the limit it takes health itself. Doc can clear it.

pages.title: The hot-spring cave
pages.text: A lit trail runs east off the highway to it. White saltpeter crusts the walls of the way down, and yellow sulfur rims the pool: mine both. With charcoal they make gunpowder.

pages.title: Zone 3: the works
pages.text:
Across the dam the street lamps still burn: keep to them. The control house at the dam has a logbook on the desk (right-click it). The powerhouse, the machine shop, the foundry, the rail yard and its mine are along the avenue south. Their dark halves are not empty.

The foundry's crucible and the machine shop's old lathe come away with a pick, for home.

pages.title: The grey ones
pages.text:
By day, and in lamplight, they are slow and half blind: they see a few paces, only in front, and do not hear a walk. In the dark they are fast and see all round. Keep to the light, and walk: they hear running and shots through walls, a walk or a pick only with nothing between.

They give a rattle before they come, and strike with one lunge you can see: it rears, then throws itself at where you stood. Step aside. No more than three hunt at once.

They nest in the dark halves of the buildings, the engine shed and the mine. By night they come out to their doors. Killed, others drift in by dawn. With one hunting close, holding H does nothing. They never come into the valley, onto the dam, or east of the gorge.

pages.title: The ridge
pages.text:
Past the gate the ground itself is poison: without a suit, on the road, the limit comes in about eight seconds, and death soon after. Off the road it is worse; indoors, less.

The hazard suit, carried in the pack, lets almost nothing through: on the road the limit is minutes away, enough to walk up and back. Watch the meter.

Blue tablets bind thirty of the dose: right-click to take one. There are some in the refuge on the pass.

pages.title: Meeting Ray
pages.text: Four canvas, four lead, a glass and two charcoal at the workbench make the hazard suit, or Ray will sell one. The phone now has a row to ask Ray to meet you at the refuge on the pass; he comes only once you carry the suit. He waits there by day, six to six, in an orange suit: right-click him. Make room in your pack first.

pages.title: Solar power
pages.text:
A solar array (four panels, four wiring, four planks, eight nails) works only at home, under open sky: the balcony, the valley floor, or the cliff above. Under rock or a roof it makes nothing. It makes the most at noon and nothing from six in the evening to six in the morning.

A battery bank (six battery cells, four wiring, two planks, six nails) keeps the power through the night. Right-click any of them to see how it is doing.

pages.title: The rig, the fridge, the pump
pages.text:
A mining rig (two graphics cards, a power supply, a board, two wiring) earns sats into the hot wallet while it has power. My computer shows what it has mined, today and in all. Two arrays and a bank run one rig day and night. A second rig needs a hydro generator.

The fridge (a fridge unit, two wiring, two planks, four nails) turns a water jug in it to cold water each hour it has power; cold water mends a little. The water pump (a pump unit, two wiring, two pipe fittings, two planks): right-click it to fill every empty jug you carry. When power runs short the rig stops first.

pages.title: Making rounds
pages.text:
A powder mill (four cobble, four planks, six nails, two iron): two saltpeter, a charcoal and a sulfur make two gunpowder. At the forge, two iron and a stick make a bullet mold; a lead and a coal or charcoal cast eight bullets.

At the workbench a gunpowder, four casings, four bullets and four primers make four pistol rounds; with two gunpowder, four rifle rounds. Casings do not come back: find more (the faction's patrols carry a few).

pages.title: Steel, and the lathe
pages.text:
The crucible furnace (the foundry's crucible, eight cobble, four clay, two iron): two steel stock and a coal make two steel, or two iron and two coal make one. Steel stock comes from the works' racks, rails and crates.

The lathe (the old lathe's parts, four steel, two wiring, two planks) fits found guns: a pistol becomes a quiet one, the raiders' rifle a good one. It also makes plate armour (the vest, four steel, two leather), which stops half of every blow from the pack, and a steel pickaxe.

pages.title: The hydro generator
pages.text:
Ray's drawings, bought by phone, show how: turbine parts, six steel and four wiring at the workbench, with the sluice tools (kept). The parts are in the powerhouse's crate and its tool locker.

Set it at home in the creek, at the water's edge: it turns two kilowatts day and night, rain or shine. With it, more than one rig runs; three at once is a farm.

pages.title: The uplink
pages.text:
Three things and power. The antenna (three dish sections from the tower yard, four steel, two wiring, two pipe fittings): hold it and right-click the hoist in the balcony's north corner, and it goes up onto the cliff. The telescope (the observatory's optics, two steel, a glass, two planks, at the lathe), set at home under open sky: right-click to look, move the mouse to aim, E to step back. The terminal (Ray's modem, two rare components, four wiring, with the plans): hold it and right-click my computer.

Fit the terminal and the computer has an Uplink page. With the antenna up, the telescope set and a generator turning in the creek, the link opens. Ask it things: each answer puts something on the map, on the screen when you are out, or among what you can make.

pages.title: Medicine
pages.text: The medical bench and the distiller work only while a generator turns. At the distiller four corn or four potatoes, a jug of water and a charcoal make spirit. At the bench: blue tablets (spirit, iron, two herbs, a charcoal), antibiotics that mend you as far as your dose allows (spirit, three herbs, honey), and adrenaline (spirit, four coffee beans, salt): for a minute blows hurt half as much.

pages.title: Its drawings
pages.text: The uplink sends one drawing every six hours. The thermal optic, carried, shows warm bodies while you focus (Q). A sonic lure, set down and right-clicked, wails for forty seconds and draws them to it. A smoke pot burns for a minute and none of them will step within eight paces. Engineer's armour, from plate armour, stops most of a blow.
